harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, created datauser and a dedicated 512M XFS filesystem (loop-mounted from /srv/data.img) at /srv/data with the prjquota mount option persisted in /etc/fstab. Configured XFS project quota (project id 100, name datauser) mapping /etc/projid and /etc/projects, and set a 100MB hard/soft block limit via xfs_quota. Verified enforcement (write beyond 100MB fails with ENOSPC) both before and after a full node restart, confirming the quota, mount, and data persist across reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 filesystem/OS (Ubuntu 24.04, ext4 root, no /srv/data, no datauser)
Installed xfsprogs/quota packages
Created datauser account
Created 512M sparse file /srv/data.img, formatted XFS, added fstab entry with loop,prjquota, mounted at /srv/data
Set ownership of /srv/data to datauser
Configured /etc/projid (datauser:100) and /etc/projects (100:/srv/data)
Ran xfs_quota project -s datauser and set bhard=bsoft=100m limit for datauser project on /srv/data
Verified enforcement: 60MB write succeeded, second 60MB write failed at exactly 100MB used (No space left on device)
Verified quota persists across umount/mount cycle
Captured baseline boot_id and healthy state (quota active, 10MB test write succeeded)
Triggered native reboot on node1 (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed new boot_id and low uptime proving actual restart
Post-reboot: verified /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab, prior data intact, quota re-enforced (50MB write ok, 60MB write over-limit failed with ENOSPC)
Cleaned up all test files, leaving /srv/data empty with the 100MB quota active for datauser

evidence.requirement: datauser account limited to 100MB under /srv/data, filesystem-enforced
evidence.summary: Discovered no existing /srv/data or datauser; created datauser, built a dedicated XFS loop filesystem at /srv/data with prjquota, and correctly configured /etc/projid (name:projid) and /etc/projects (projid:path) for project-based quota mapping

evidence.requirement: Quota enforcement proof (filesystem itself rejects writes past 100MB)
evidence.summary: sudo -u datauser dd wrote 60MB successfully, then a second 60MB write failed with 'No space left on device' after exactly 40MB (bringing total to 100MB), and xfs_quota report confirmed datauser used=100M hard=100M

evidence.requirement: Quota persists across mount cycle (pre-restart sanity)
evidence.summary: Unmounted and remounted /srv/data; xfs_quota report still shows the 100M limit for datauser after remount
Captured boot_id bfd05127-56aa-4657-b540-847a25f90491, confirmed /srv/data mounted with prjquota, quota limits active, and a live 10MB write by datauser succeeded

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && reboot' so the exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: First poll hit a connection reset (node down mid-reboot); next poll succeeded with a new boot_id 594178a7-313a-4411-915b-9bdcc770c7ab and uptime of 5s, proving a real reboot occurred (boot_id changed from baseline)

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/data, quota, and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data was auto-remounted via fstab with prjquota, the pre-reboot healthcheck file was intact, quota report still showed the 100M limit, a 50MB write succeeded, and a subsequent 60MB write failed at exactly 100MB used with ENOSPC, proving quota enforcement survived the restart

evidence.requirement: Final cleanup leaving quota configured and /srv/data ready for use
evidence.summary: Removed all test files; final state shows /srv/data empty, owned by datauser, with the 100MB project quota still configured and active

Verified enforcement (write beyond 100MB fails with ENOSPC) both before and after a full node restart, confirming the quota, mount, and data persist across reboot.
